newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ross back in Middle East to broker Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Ross back in Middle East to broker Hebron deal.

text.p: U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross has launched a new bid to broker an elusive Hebron accord between Israel and the PLO, but the Palestinians are showing signs of mistrust.
Ross travelled to the Gaza Strip late on Saturday for talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat after meeting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem.
Earlier in the day, Israeli soldiers clashed with hundreds of Palestinians in the West Bank town of Hebron. Witnesses said two Arabs beaten by soldiers were rushed to a hospital.

The violence erupted after Jewish settlers scuffled with Palestinian school children in the town, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence. Soldiers intervened, arresting at least two Palestinians and clearing demonstrators from the approach to one of the Jewish enclaves in Hebron.
Ross, whose last mediation effort collapsed in October, was to bring new ideas for bridging the gaps between Israelis and Palestinians on the long overdue Israeli withdrawal from Hebron.
But Palestinians were concerned he may be favouring Israel.
"We want him (Ross) to be on the side of the agreement, not on the side of Israel," PLO official Hassan Asfour told Reuters.
The United States, sponsor of Israeli-Arab peace talks launched in 1991, has pressed both sides to finalise their accord on Hebron and proceed to talks on an overall peace deal.

Palestinians were encouraged when President Bill Clinton criticised Israel's expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank last week but U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher's comments on Thursday that Palestinians had to make concessions on Hebron irked PLO leaders.
An Israeli legislator who met with Yasser Arafat said the Palestinian president wanted Ross replaced.

"He (Arafat) said he's ready for mediation or arbitration as long as it is not done by Dennis Ross," said Yossi Beilin, a key figure in peace talks that led to the breakthrough Israel-PLO peace in 1993.

Beilin, whose Labour party was ousted by hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in elections last May, met Arafat in the Gaza Strip on Friday. He said the Palestinian leader did not explain his objection to Ross.

"I said to him that that would be his biggest mistake, that the United States is the sponsor and Dennis Ross is its representative and even if he would like to have others, the best thing that he could do is to accept Ross as a mediator because that's the only way to make progress in the Hebron talks," Beilin told Reuters.

Arafat, who says no progress has been made in talks since October, said on Friday: "The most important thing is that Mr Ross has to be an accurate mediator, and not to be biased on the side of Israel."

The U.S. administration last sent Ross after clashes in September in the West Bank and Gaza killed 15 Israeli soldiers and 60 Palestinians. He left after three weeks saying the two sides had narrowed the gaps but failed to reach a deal.

Christopher had put the onus for progress on Arafat on Thursday, saying Israel had "made some moves" over Hebron and it was up to the Palestinians to respond. He also announced the return of Ross to Israel.
Israelis and Palestinians accuse each other of foot-dragging in talks on Hebron.

Arafat has demanded Israel implement the partial withdrawal agreement it signed more than a year ago. Netanyahu has sought changes to protect around 400 militant Jewish settlers living among 100,000 Arabs in the town.
